# Interview Prep Packs: Practice Prompts by Track

> Practice prompts for every GenAI interview track, each with what a strong answer covers and the red flags interviewers note, keyed to roles and to the system-design archetypes.

## How to use these packs

1. **Find your track.** Your role's hub names it; the table below lists the roles on each track. Classify the actual loop with the recruiter first ([interview loops](interview-loops.md)).
2. **Practise aloud and timed.** For design prompts, use the [45-minute blueprint](system-design-archetypes.md); for behavioural prompts, the STAR-AI story bank in [behavioural calibration](behavioral-calibration.md); for coding, the formats in [coding rounds](coding-rounds.md).
3. **Score yourself** against "a strong answer covers", then check the red flags. Re-run the prompt a week later.
4. **Expect variation.** These are prompts the research reports or synthesises; real loops differ by company and level.

The packs give practice prompts and answer criteria, not model answers. Each prompt carries its source and grade (B, C, D); prompts the research does not report directly are labelled.

Classify the loop before you prepare: the three loop types drill different archetypes ([interview loops](interview-loops.md)).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AI-lab infrastructure loop** | Anthropic; OpenAI infrastructure and inference teams | A1, A2, A3, A4, A5 | A7, A14 | Expect numbers early, 50–60 minute rounds and failure-mode probing; Anthropic rounds have shown a design-document review variant. | T0-14 L119 |
| **Applied-AI / AI-engineer loop** | Databricks, Google GenAI, scale-ups, Meta ML | A8, A9, A10, A11, A12, A13, A14, A15 | — | Drill RAG, assistant, copilot, agent, voice, extraction, eval and safety designs first. | T0-14 L120 |
| **Classic loop with AI flavour** | Meta and Google SWE, Stripe, Uber | A8, A9 | — | Keep classic design sharp; prepare one or two LLM-flavoured prompts (A8, A9) as insurance, and be ready to place an LLM component sensibly. | T0-14 L121 |

## The packs

### Application pack

*What it tests:* RAG with access control, agent loop control, evaluation architecture, context management. *Source:* career/02-roles/role-catalog.md §8.2 (T1-03, T0-14).

#### p001 · A8 Enterprise RAG / permission-aware search (including multimodal documents)

> How would you build an LLM-powered enterprise search system?

- **Source:** OpenAI (2026 Glassdoor review); OpenAI's PracHub ML-design pool adds low-latency RAG and an enterprise RAG assistant for internal documents [C · T0-14 L359]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L360, L385–386, L563, L572, L753):
  - Elicit corpus size and modalities, the ACL model, freshness, QPS, latency budget, citation requirement, accuracy bar and the cost of a wrong answer
  - ACL enforcement as a retrieval-time, fail-closed invariant: pre-filter at the index, re-check at context assembly
  - Hybrid BM25 plus dense retrieval with rank fusion and a reranker, each stage proven on recall@k
  - Retrieval (recall@k) evaluated separately from generation (faithfulness)
  - An embedding-model migration plan; re-embedding also invalidates any semantic cache
  - Untrusted content and sensitive data kept from meeting in one context without egress control (the EchoLeak lesson)
- **Red flags:**
  - ACL post-filtering, which leaks and wastes top-k
  - Permissions enforced in the prompt
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** RAG, Permission-aware retrieval (ACLs, tenancy), Hybrid search (BM25 + dense), Reranking, Retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR, nDCG), Embedding & reranker models

#### p002 · A8 Enterprise RAG / permission-aware search (including multimodal documents)

> Design distributed search over about 1 billion documents.

- **Source:** Anthropic (the most consistently reported design prompt, per IGotAnOffer) [C · T0-14 L359]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L193, L385, L563, L651, L740, L802):
  - Vector memory = vectors × dimensions × bytes: 1B vectors at 1,024 dimensions take about 4.1 TB in fp32, 1.0 TB in int8 and 0.13 TB with product quantisation
  - Recall versus latency, ACL correctness and freshness
  - Hybrid BM25 plus dense retrieval with rank fusion; a reranker only where top-k precision matters and the latency budget allows
  - Per-tenant indices or namespaces with an ACL pre-filter that fails closed
  - Re-embedding migration when the embedding model changes
- **Red flags:**
  - Never quantifies
  - ACL post-filtering, which leaks and wastes top-k
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Embeddings & vector search, ANN indexes (HNSW, IVF, PQ), Hybrid search (BM25 + dense), Search & ranking (learning to rank), Permission-aware retrieval (ACLs, tenancy), System design

#### p003 · A8 Enterprise RAG / permission-aware search (including multimodal documents)

> Design retrieval and reranking for coding agents.

- **Source:** Databricks (one reported SWE phone screen) [C · T0-14 L359; L175]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L385, L420, L429, L563, L810):
  - Hybrid retrieval with rank fusion where the corpus has identifiers, jargon or exact terms; a reranker when top-k precision matters and latency allows
  - Context ranked from open files, symbols and recent edits
  - Rerank latency versus recall; context size versus time to first token
  - Each retrieval stage proven on recall@k before it is added
- **Red flags:**
  - Surface-level technology choices with no reason or number behind them
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Retrieval quality (hybrid, reranking, recall@k), Hybrid search (BM25 + dense), Reranking, Retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR, nDCG), Context engineering

#### p004 · A8 Enterprise RAG / permission-aware search (including multimodal documents)

> Take-home: answer questions over about 50 documents and report recall@5 and faithfulness on a 20-question set.

- **Source:** Applied-AI startup take-home (described in one write-up) [D · T0-06 L318]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L379, L385–386, L563, L712, L716, L724):
  - Retrieval (recall@k) measured separately from generation (faithfulness)
  - Questions unambiguous enough that two experts would agree on pass or fail, with positive and negative cases
  - Hybrid BM25 plus dense retrieval and a reranker, each stage proven on recall@k before it is added
  - Chunk size and context prefixes
  - A citation and faithfulness check on every answer
- **Red flags:**
  - 'We'd test it with some prompts', or one uncalibrated LLM judge
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** RAG, Retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR, nDCG), Hybrid search (BM25 + dense), Reranking, Grounding & citations (hallucination control), Golden datasets & test-set curation

#### p005 · A9 ChatGPT-style assistant with context assembly and memory

> Design a ChatGPT-style chat assistant at high scale, with context assembly and memory.

- **Source:** Anthropic (chat system: 7 of 112 AceOffer reports); OpenAI (high-scale chat application); DesignGurus ('Design ChatGPT'); Meta's ML pool (LLM-based conversational assistant) [B · T0-14 L390; L173]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L391, L409–410, L804, L807):
  - Elicit DAU and concurrent streams, context length, tools, memory scope and deletion rules, moderation and multi-device sync
  - Cache-friendly prompt layout (static prefix first) and how it drives prefix-cache hit rate and cost
  - Summarisation or compaction versus a sliding window, tuned for recall first
  - Memory governance: write policy (supersession, contradiction), what is stored and who can delete it
  - Moderating a stream without blocking time to first token; SSE versus WebSocket
  - Server-side state versus client re-send
- **Red flags:**
  - Ignores streaming and latency physics (TTFT versus TPOT)
  - No evaluation story ('we'd test it')
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Context engineering, Agent memory & state, Prefix caching & KV reuse, Guardrails, Server-Sent Events (SSE), Streaming & agent UX

#### p006 · A9 ChatGPT-style assistant with context assembly and memory

> Design a customer-support chatbot on a third-party LLM platform.

- **Source:** Aced (formerly Exponent) list of 2026 prompts [C · T0-14 L390]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L397, L574, L586, L712, L719, L770, L805–806):
  - Requirements first: whether it acts or only answers, knowledge source and freshness, quality bar and the cost of a wrong answer
  - Context assembly: static prefix first, then memory, then trimmed history
  - Input moderation before generation, streamed output moderation with a small lag buffer, and a post-hoc audit pass
  - A golden set drawn from real failures, with production traffic sampled through the same graders
  - What happens when the provider is down or a model version changes behaviour
- **Red flags:**
  - Treats the LLM as a source of truth, with no validation
  - Hand-wavy safety
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [Forward Deployed Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/forward-deployed-engineer.md), [AI / GenAI Solutions Architect](../02-roles/hubs/ai-solutions-architect.md)
- **Skills probed:** LLM APIs & tool calling, Context engineering, Guardrails, LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates), Model selection & routing

#### p007 · A10 Latency-critical code completion plus coding assistant

> Design an LLM-based coding assistant, including latency-critical inline code completion.

- **Source:** Meta (ML system design pool); code-completion design in coach lists [C · T0-14 L414]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L415, L420–421, L429–430, L807):
  - Elicit the inline-completion latency budget (coach sources suggest a few hundred milliseconds), keystroke-rate bursts, code privacy and telemetry
  - A small model close to the user versus a large central model; prefix KV reuse as the user types
  - Context size versus time to first token, with context ranked from open files, symbols and recent edits
  - Speculative decoding, which helps most at low-to-medium QPS
  - Retained-after-N-seconds beats raw acceptance; execution-based offline evals paired with online retention metrics
  - Capacity planned for keystroke bursts
- **Red flags:**
  - Ignores streaming and latency physics (TTFT versus TPOT)
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Cost & latency engineering, Speculative decoding, Prefix caching & KV reuse, Context engineering, Online evaluation & production monitoring, Agent-UX telemetry

#### p008 · A11 Long-running tool-using agent platform

> Design an agent system that executes tasks for users from a chat interface.

- **Source:** OpenAI (Aug 2026 Glassdoor review); variants: Anthropic (an agent system that adapts to new tasks), Meta's ML pool (agentic ticket investigation), Google Cloud GenAI forward-deployed engineer loops (agentic system design) [C · T0-14 L434; L173]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L435, L445–446, L452–454, L570, L652, L724, L733):
  - Elicit side-effect classes (read-only, reversible, irreversible), budgets (steps, tokens, wall-clock), concurrency, tenancy and human-approval policy
  - Blast radius first (Rule of Two): at most two of untrusted input, sensitive access and the ability to act externally, otherwise human approval
  - Idempotent tools and a resumable loop: an append-only event log and checkpoints
  - A deterministic workflow by default; an agent only where the path cannot be predetermined; sub-agents only to isolate context
  - Reliability over repeated trials: pass^k (0.75 per trial gives about 42% for three in a row)
  - The eval harness built before agent features
- **Red flags:**
  - An unbounded loop with no budgets
  - Grading only the agent's final answer
- **Roles:** [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md), [Forward Deployed Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/forward-deployed-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Agents & tool use, Agent reliability (durable state, budgets, approvals), Durable execution & workflow state, Human-in-the-loop design, Agent evaluation (trajectories, task success), Containment (DLP, sandboxing, egress)

#### p009 · A11 Long-running tool-using agent platform

> Agent-debugging round: an agent fails on a task; find out why and fix it.

- **Source:** No fixed prompt reported (D): agent-debugging rounds are reported in applied-AI startup loops; the wording is this repository's [D · T0-06 L318]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L435, L442, L454, L714, L717, L719, L724, L764, L767):
  - Read the trace first: turns, tool calls, tokens and latency, with prompt and model versions and replay
  - Grade the outcome (end state), not the exact tool-call path
  - Several trials per task, because outputs are non-deterministic; report pass^k
  - Check the loop budgets and the tool router: schema validation, authorisation and idempotency keys
  - Turn the failure into a new eval task
- **Red flags:**
  - An unbounded loop with no budgets
  - Grading only the agent's final answer
- **Roles:** [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Agent evaluation (trajectories, task success), LLM tracing, Agent reliability (durable state, budgets, approvals), Error analysis, Eval statistics (CIs, power, pass^k)

#### p010 · A12 Real-time voice assistant

> Design a real-time AI voice system.

- **Source:** PracHub software-engineer ML-design pool; Meta (ML pool); listicles [C · T0-14 L458; L173]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L459, L475–476, L663, L807):
  - Elicit the end-to-end latency target (most vendor sources say about 800 ms voice-to-voice, range about 300–1,000 ms), telephony versus WebRTC, barge-in, languages and cost per minute
  - A per-stage p95 budget that sums to the target: network, endpointing, STT, LLM time to first token, TTS first audio
  - Overlapped stages: partial STT streamed into the LLM, sentences chunked into TTS
  - Cascaded STT, LLM and TTS (observable, swappable) versus speech-to-speech (lower latency, less control)
  - Endpointing aggressiveness and interruption semantics
- **Red flags:**
  - Stage latencies added in sequence with no overlap (one vendor's illustrative sequential budget reaches about 1,180 ms)
  - Ignores streaming and latency physics (TTFT versus TPOT)
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Speech & voice AI (ASR, TTS, realtime voice agents), Cost & latency engineering, Streaming & agent UX, Load testing & latency SLOs

#### p011 · A13 Document / multimodal ingestion and extraction at scale

> Design a document-processing pipeline that ingests heterogeneous documents for LLM use.

- **Source:** Databricks; listicles add very long document summarisation and extraction with reliability targets [C · T0-14 L480]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L481, L495, L499–500, L806):
  - Elicit volume per day, document types and lengths, field-level accuracy target, turnaround and human-review capacity
  - Cost per correct document, not per document
  - A small-model-first cascade with escalation versus an upfront router (savings vary 35–85% by workload)
  - Schema-constrained decoding versus post-validation; OCR versus a vision LLM
  - Single-pass long context versus chunked map-reduce (long context degrades mid-document)
  - Versioned outputs so a model or prompt change can be re-run safely; the batch API for non-urgent work
- **Red flags:**
  - Treats the LLM as a source of truth, with no validation
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Document ingestion, parsing & chunking, Structured output & tool schemas, Constrained decoding, Model selection & routing, Multimodal AI (vision, documents, audio), Cost & latency engineering

#### p012 · A15 Safety, abuse and prompt-injection defence architecture

> Design a malware-analysis system.

- **Source:** Anthropic (Hello Interview's Anthropic Staff list) [B · T0-14 L526]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L527, L537, L543–544, L745, L753, L755, L814):
  - Trust boundaries first: what content is untrusted, sensitive assets, irreversible actions, tenancy and false-positive tolerance
  - Design for compromise: blast-radius analysis, kill switches, an audit trail and incident response
  - Sandboxing and egress control (a domain allowlist, no auto-rendered URLs)
  - Classifiers as one layer of defence in depth, measured with adaptive attacks rather than static prompt sets
  - False positives versus missed attacks
- **Red flags:**
  - 'Add guardrails' with no placement by layer
  - Drops classic engineering (queues, retries, idempotency) once a model appears
- **Roles:** [AI Security Engineer / AI Red Teamer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-security-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Containment (DLP, sandboxing, egress), Threat modelling for AI systems, Red-teaming, Incident response & SIEM, LLM security (prompt injection, OWASP)

#### p013 · A15 Safety, abuse and prompt-injection defence architecture

> Design an LLM API with a safety layer.

- **Source:** Anthropic (coaching and aggregator pages) [C · T0-14 L526]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L527, L543, L574, L731, L737–747, L753):
  - Controls placed by layer: ingestion, retrieval, context assembly, model, tool gateway, output, egress, cost and abuse, response
  - Input moderated before generation; streamed output moderated with a small lag buffer; a post-hoc audit pass
  - Output treated as untrusted input downstream: schema validation, auto-rendering markdown and links stripped, PII and secret filters
  - Token-based rate limits, max output tokens and per-tenant budgets (OWASP LLM10)
  - False positives versus missed attacks, and the response-time overhead
- **Red flags:**
  - 'Tell the model to ignore malicious instructions'
  - A static benchmark score offered as proof that a defence works
- **Roles:** [AI Security Engineer / AI Red Teamer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-security-engineer.md), [Responsible AI / AI Governance Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/responsible-ai-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Guardrails, LLM security (prompt injection, OWASP), OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, PII detection & redaction, Production hardening (rate limits, spend caps, kill switches)

#### p014 · A15 Safety, abuse and prompt-injection defence architecture

> Design safeguards for an AI system that can take actions on behalf of a user.

- **Source:** Aced (formerly Exponent) list of 2026 prompts [C · T0-14 L526]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L95, L733, L743, L745, L747, L753, L755, L757):
  - Trust-boundary analysis with the Rule of Two: untrusted input, sensitive access, ability to act externally; if all three are needed, split the agent or add approval
  - Assume the injection succeeds and bound the blast radius
  - Permissions in the tool gateway and retrieval layer, not the prompt: least privilege, scoped short-lived credentials, allowlists, human approval for irreversible actions
  - Egress control: a domain allowlist and proxy, no data-bearing URLs
  - A kill switch, audit log and incident runbook; adaptive red-team evals in CI
- **Red flags:**
  - Classifier-only defence: adaptive attacks bypassed 12 published defences with over 90% success in most cases
  - Permissions enforced in the prompt
- **Roles:** [AI Security Engineer / AI Red Teamer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-security-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Responsible AI / AI Governance Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/responsible-ai-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Prompt-injection attack & defence, Containment (DLP, sandboxing, egress), Agent abuse & MCP authorisation, Human-in-the-loop design, Red-teaming, OAuth/OIDC, RBAC, SSO

#### p015

> How would you reduce hallucinations in an LLM application?

- **Source:** Dataford GenAI-engineer aggregate (12 guides) [C · T0-14 L104]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L379, L386, L565, L716, L806, L875; T1-03 L194):
  - Answers grounded in retrieved sources, with a citation and faithfulness check
  - Validators, citations and fallbacks rather than trusting the model
  - Retrieval (recall@k) evaluated separately from generation (faithfulness, groundedness)
  - Retrieve when the corpus exceeds the window, changes often or needs per-user ACLs; fine-tune for style or format, not for facts that change
  - Guardrails, confidence thresholds and fallbacks instead of promising 100% accuracy
- **Red flags:**
  - Treats the LLM as a source of truth, with no validation
  - Assumes a bigger context window removes the need for retrieval
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md), [AI Evaluation Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-evaluation-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Grounding & citations (hallucination control), RAG, Retrieval metrics (recall@k, MRR, nDCG), Guardrails, Choosing RAG vs long context vs fine-tuning, LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates)

#### p016

> What is your approach to fine-tuning? When would you fine-tune rather than prompt or retrieve?

- **Source:** Dataford GenAI-engineer aggregate (12 guides) [C · T0-14 L104]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L562, L565, L625; T0-06 L496):
  - Prompt and retrieve first; fine-tune or distil when the task is narrow, stable and high-volume, a small model must hit a latency or cost target, and a golden set exists to prove parity
  - Fine-tune for style or format, not for facts that change; retrieve for large, changing or permissioned knowledge
  - The price gap between small and frontier models, quoted as ratios rather than memorised prices
  - A regression eval budgeted for every base-model upgrade
- **Red flags:**
  - Fine-tuning before showing that prompting and retrieval fail
  - Fine-tuning to inject facts that change
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md), [Applied Scientist](../02-roles/hubs/applied-scientist.md)
- **Skills probed:** Choosing RAG vs long context vs fine-tuning, Fine-tuning (SFT, LoRA), Model selection & routing, Golden datasets & test-set curation, Cost & latency engineering

#### p023 · A1 Multi-tenant LLM inference API / serving platform

> Design an inference API for serving LLMs.

- **Source:** Anthropic (41 of 112 AceOffer reports); close variants in Databricks' GenAI-engineer track and Meta's ML pool [B · T0-14 L206; L173]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L207, L227–229, L646–647):
  - Elicit tenants and priority tiers, peak RPS, input and output token distributions, streaming, TTFT p99 and TPOT targets, model sizes and a cost target
  - Goodput as the SLO: requests per second per GPU that meet both TTFT and TPOT
  - Capacity from KV-cache maths: KV bytes per token = 2 × layers × KV heads × head dim × bytes per element, then concurrency per node
  - Continuous batching with paged KV; colocated versus disaggregated prefill and decode
  - Admission control and load shedding; autoscaling on queue depth and KV utilisation, with a warm pool
  - Tenant fairness and a canary rollout behind an eval gate
- **Red flags:**
  - One request per GPU
  - Autoscaling on CPU
  - No distinction between prefill and decode
- **Roles:** [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md), [GPU Kernel / ML Compiler Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/gpu-kernel-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Serving literacy (vLLM, batching, quantisation), Continuous batching & KV cache, Prefill/decode disaggregation, Inference autoscaling, Load testing & latency SLOs, Capacity & GPU/API cost governance

#### p024 · A1 Multi-tenant LLM inference API / serving platform

> Design a token-generation service that handles about 100K requests per second.

- **Source:** Anthropic [C · T0-14 L206]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L228, L643, L647, L649–650, L700, L802):
  - Traffic first: average and peak requests per second, then input and output tokens per second
  - Concurrent streams by Little's law (streams = arrival rate × time in system), then nodes at the per-node concurrency limit
  - Per-node concurrency = (HBM − weights − overhead) ÷ (KV bytes per token × context length)
  - Output length dominates latency: E2E = TTFT + (output tokens − 1) × inter-token latency
  - Goodput under TTFT and TPOT SLOs, not raw throughput
- **Red flags:**
  - Never quantifies
  - Correct arithmetic with no design consequence ('so it's a lot')
- **Roles:** [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md), [GPU Kernel / ML Compiler Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/gpu-kernel-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Capacity & GPU/API cost governance, Continuous batching & KV cache, Load testing & latency SLOs, GPU fundamentals (HBM, prefill vs decode), Serving literacy (vLLM, batching, quantisation)

#### p025 · A2 GPU request-batching service

> Design an end-to-end batching system for LLM inference requests (one reported variant: 100 requests should take about the same time as one).

- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L234, L248–250):
  - Elicit max batch size, latency SLO, arrival rate and burstiness, input-length variance, and cancellation and timeout semantics
  - Static batching with a timer versus dynamic versus continuous (iteration-level) batching
  - Max wait derived from the latency budget (arrival rate × max wait approximates batch fill)
  - Length bucketing to cut padding; head-of-line blocking from long prompts
  - A bounded queue with backpressure, and correct demultiplexing of results under partial failure
  - Poison requests and cancellation
- **Red flags:**
  - No bound on the queue
  - No answer for 'one request in the batch fails'
- **Roles:** [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md), [GPU Kernel / ML Compiler Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/gpu-kernel-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md)

#### p031 · A6 LLM gateway / internal AI platform

> Design a prompt caching and retrieval system.

- **Source:** Anthropic (SWE candidates, per IGotAnOffer) [C · T0-14 L316]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L98, L567, L645, L661, L869, L871):
  - Cache layers in order: prefix (prompt) cache, then exact-match cache, then a semantic cache only on low-stakes, high-repeat, non-personalised routes
  - Prefix caching needs an exact prefix match: static content first and breakpoints at stable boundaries, with the hit rate verified
  - Prompt-cache economics: break-even reads per write = (w − 1) ÷ (1 − r), so one read repays a write at the multipliers quoted in October 2026
  - Semantic-cache hygiene: per-route thresholds, keys scoped by tenant and by prompt and model version, invalidation on embedding-model change
  - Semantic-cache value net of the cost of false hits
- **Red flags:**
  - A cache breakpoint on changing content, such as a timestamp, causing perpetual misses and repeated write charges
  - A semantic cache whose false-hit rate is never measured
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md), [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Prefix caching & KV reuse, Semantic & prompt caching, Cost & latency engineering, LLM gateways, Embeddings & vector search

#### p033

> Roofline analysis: is LLM prefill or decode compute-bound or memory-bound, and why?

- **Source:** Anthropic (4 of 112 AceOffer reports) [B · T0-14 L551]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L89, L229, L551, L634, L648, L658, L882):
  - Arithmetic intensity: decode at batch 1 is about 1 FLOP per byte, against an H100 ridge point of roughly 300 FLOP per byte (989 TFLOPS ÷ 3.35 TB/s)
  - Prefill is compute-bound and decode memory-bound, so goodput is the SLO metric
  - Decode ceiling: minimum time per output token = (weights + active KV) ÷ total memory bandwidth; real systems reach a fraction of it (MBU)
  - Prefill time ≈ 2 × parameters × input tokens ÷ (peak FLOPs × MFU)
  - Dense versus with-sparsity FLOPs checked before any spec-sheet number is used
- **Red flags:**
  - Uses the with-sparsity H100 figure (1,979 TFLOPS) as the dense BF16 number
  - No distinction between prefill and decode
- **Roles:** [GPU Kernel / ML Compiler Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/gpu-kernel-engineer.md), [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** GPU fundamentals (HBM, prefill vs decode), Profiling & roofline (Nsight), GPU memory performance, Continuous batching & KV cache, Serving literacy (vLLM, batching, quantisation)

#### p034

> p95 latency has jumped from about 100 ms to about 2,000 ms. Debug it.

- **Source:** Anthropic (one report: a debugging exercise inside the design round) [C · T0-14 L552]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L552; T1-03 L223):
  - Segment by percentile and cohort before guessing
  - Split latency into queue, prefill and decode
  - Check batch size, KV-cache pressure and long-context outliers
  - Check retries and timeouts, a shift in cache-hit rate, a noisy neighbour and the diff of the last deploy
- **Red flags:**
  - Guessing without data
  - Not forming hypotheses
- **Roles:** [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md), [GPU Kernel / ML Compiler Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/gpu-kernel-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Load testing & latency SLOs, Observability (OpenTelemetry traces, metrics), Continuous batching & KV cache, SRE (SLOs, on-call, incidents)

*What it tests:* golden sets, judge calibration, online sampling, A/B tests. *Source:* career/02-roles/role-catalog.md §8.2 (T1-03, T0-14).

#### p035 · A14 LLM/agent evaluation platform and observability

> How would you evaluate an LLM system?

- **Source:** Dataford GenAI-engineer aggregate (its most frequent question, in 19 guides) [C · T0-14 L104; L504]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L573, L711–714, L717–719, L724):
  - Success defined from the cost of a wrong answer, mapped from business metric to proxy to offline metric
  - A golden set of 20–50 tasks from real failures, unambiguous enough that two experts agree, with positive and negative cases
  - Capability suites kept separate from regression suites, with saturation watched
  - Code graders where outcomes are checkable, an LLM judge calibrated against humans elsewhere, humans to calibrate
  - Several trials per task, with pass^k for user-facing reliability
  - A CI gate on regressions, and production traffic sampled through the same graders
- **Red flags:**
  - 'We'd test it with some prompts'
  - One uncalibrated LLM judge, or a model judging its own outputs
  - No regression gate and no production feedback loop
- **Roles:** [AI Evaluation Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-evaluation-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [Applied Scientist](../02-roles/hubs/applied-scientist.md), [Domain Evaluation Specialist / AI Trainer](../02-roles/hubs/domain-evaluation-specialist.md)
- **Skills probed:** LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates), Golden datasets & test-set curation, LLM-as-judge design & calibration, Eval statistics (CIs, power, pass^k), Eval regression gates in CI, Online evaluation & production monitoring

#### p036 · A14 LLM/agent evaluation platform and observability

> Design a model evaluation and monitoring system (one variant: run evaluation benchmarks across hundreds of model variants).

- **Source:** Anthropic (SWE candidates, per IGotAnOffer; the benchmark variant comes from one aggregator) [C · T0-14 L504]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L505, L510, L521–522, L720, L724):
  - Elicit number of teams and agents, trial cost, grader mix, CI integration and production sampling
  - Sandboxed runners with a clean environment for every trial
  - Code versus LLM versus human graders (cost, determinism, nuance), with judge versions pinned
  - Trials versus cost (the batch API for offline runs); static versus rolling datasets (saturation, contamination)
  - Flaky-task detection, and tests for the eval itself: one reported benchmark score moved from 42% to 95% once grader bugs were fixed
  - Ownership: the platform owns infrastructure, product teams contribute tasks; eval metrics tied to business outcomes
- **Red flags:**
  - One uncalibrated LLM judge
  - No regression gate and no production feedback loop
- **Roles:** [AI Evaluation Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-evaluation-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md), [Research Engineer / Member of Technical Staff](../02-roles/hubs/research-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates), Benchmark construction, LLM-as-judge design & calibration, Eval regression gates in CI, Online evaluation & production monitoring, Observability (OpenTelemetry traces, metrics)

#### p037 · A14 LLM/agent evaluation platform and observability

> Design an evaluation platform for many agent workflows.

- **Source:** Staff-level listicles [C · T0-14 L504]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L522, L605, L607, L652, L714, L717, L724):
  - Trajectories and outcomes evaluated over repeated trials
  - The outcome (end state) graded, not the exact tool-call path
  - pass@k versus pass^k, and chained steps multiplying (0.98 per step over 20 steps is about 67%)
  - A clean, isolated environment for every trial
  - Trial isolation and grader calibration as the two deep dives
  - Ownership: the platform owns infrastructure, product teams contribute tasks
- **Red flags:**
  - Grading only the agent's final answer
- **Roles:** [AI Evaluation Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-evaluation-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** Agent evaluation (trajectories, task success), Eval statistics (CIs, power, pass^k), LLM-as-judge design & calibration, LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates), LLM tracing

#### p038 · A14 LLM/agent evaluation platform and observability

> Evaluation discussion: when would you use an LLM judge, and when human annotation?

- **Source:** Google (ML-platform and GenAI design rounds, where this discussion is reported as central) [C · T0-14 L174]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L573, L714–715, L724):
  - Code graders first, LLM judges where needed, humans to calibrate
  - Judge validity: over 80% agreement with humans on MT-Bench-style tasks (2023, one benchmark), with position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias
  - Mitigations: swap answer order, use rubrics and references, avoid judging with the generator's model family, re-calibrate when the judge version changes
  - One dimension per judge, with an 'Unknown' option
  - Humans as the slow, costly gold standard that calibrates the rest
- **Red flags:**
  - A model judging its own outputs
  - One uncalibrated LLM judge
- **Roles:** [AI Evaluation Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-evaluation-engineer.md), [Applied Scientist](../02-roles/hubs/applied-scientist.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md), [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Domain Evaluation Specialist / AI Trainer](../02-roles/hubs/domain-evaluation-specialist.md)
- **Skills probed:** LLM-as-judge design & calibration, Human evaluation programmes, Rubrics & inter-rater agreement, Eval statistics (CIs, power, pass^k), LLM evaluation (golden sets, calibrated judges, CI gates)

#### p039

> Give a research talk on your own work (one round of a frontier-lab loop that also has coding and values rounds).

### Governance pack

*What it tests:* a scoping or solutions round, and fluency in the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO 42001. *Source:* career/02-roles/role-catalog.md §8.2 (T1-03, T0-14).

#### p040

> Scoping round: set up an AI governance programme (inventory, risk-assessment method, committee and evidence) mapped to the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001.

- **Source:** No reported prompt (D): built from the governance round in role-catalog §8.2 and the programme work described in T0-15 [D · T0-15 L162]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-15 L87, L162, L173–174, L334, L337, L342; T1-03 L178):
  - An AI inventory or registry: systems, owners, use cases and risk tiers
  - A risk-assessment method and committee operations, with one accountable programme lead and a cross-functional committee
  - Evidence as a by-product of delivery: Art. 12-style logs, evaluation reports, system documentation and incident records kept in the ML platform
  - Translation from legal text to evidence, the part of the work that is specific to compliance
  - Incident tracking and reporting, including the ability to halt a system
- **Red flags:**
  - Assumes most high-risk systems need a notified body (most Annex III points use internal control)
  - Treats ISO/IEC 42001 as a presumption of EU AI Act conformity (it gives none)
  - Dismisses guardrails as 'red tape' that slows shipping
- **Roles:** [AI Governance Programme Lead / Manager](../02-roles/hubs/ai-governance-lead.md), [AI Risk, Audit & Compliance Specialist](../02-roles/hubs/ai-risk-assurance-specialist.md), [Responsible AI / AI Governance Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/responsible-ai-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** AI inventory & risk register, GRC & risk assessment, EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, AI operating model & governance boards

### Product pack

*What it tests:* a scoping or product round. *Source:* career/02-roles/role-catalog.md §8.2 (T1-03, T0-14).

#### p041

> Product or scoping round: scope a GenAI feature or pilot, from whether to use an LLM to success metrics, an evaluation rubric and exit criteria.

- **Source:** No reported prompt (D): built from the product round in role-catalog §8.2 and the scoping round T2-01 lists for non-technical candidates [D · T2-01 L767]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L644, L711–712, L778, L791; T1-03 L176, L194):
  - The premise questioned: is an LLM needed, build or buy, what not to build; stakeholders and success metrics named
  - 'Good' defined measurably (task success, groundedness, safety, latency, cost) and mapped from business metric to proxy to offline metric, starting from the cost of a wrong answer
  - A rubric whose tasks are unambiguous enough that two domain experts reach the same verdict, with positive and negative cases
  - Token economics: cost per request and per month from input and output tokens and prices
  - A staged rollout with exit criteria (MVP, then v2)
  - Latency-versus-accuracy and cost-versus-safety trade-offs translated into business terms
- **Red flags:**
  - Over-promises accuracy instead of proposing guardrails, confidence thresholds and fallbacks
  - Uses jargon without linking decisions to user impact
- **Roles:** [AI Product Manager](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-manager.md), [Domain Evaluation Specialist / AI Trainer](../02-roles/hubs/domain-evaluation-specialist.md)
- **Skills probed:** Product sense, Metrics for non-deterministic systems, Rubrics & inter-rater agreement, Token & unit economics, Pilots & adoption measurement, Build-vs-buy & vendor evaluation

### Behavioural pack

*What it tests:* four AI-specific competencies answered in STAR-AI form (Situation, Task, Action, Result with a metric delta and a continuous-monitoring step): C1 technical pragmatism and ambiguity tolerance, C2 cross-functional communication and trade-off translation, C3 ownership, accountability and incident response, C4 responsible AI and safety consciousness. *Source:* T1-03 §6.2 L171–204.

#### p042

> Tell me about a time your model failed catastrophically in production. How did you detect it?

- **Source:** T1-03 bank (B1) [C · T1-03 L193]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T1-03 L175, L177, L186–187, L193):
  - Detection by alerts and monitoring, not by a customer complaint
  - Root-cause discipline and a postmortem artefact
  - Immediate remediation (rollback, fallback, routing) plus systemic prevention (alerts, eval pipelines)
  - What you did, not the team, ending with a metric delta and a continuous-monitoring step
- **Red flags:**
  - Deflects blame to teammates, data engineers or third-party model providers
  - Blames external factors ('the data was bad') without systematic troubleshooting

#### p055

> AI-enabled coding round: solve the task with an AI assistant in the editor.

- **Source:** Meta (spring 2026, early signal) [C · T1-03 L221]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T1-03 L221, L229–232):
  - Orient first: confirm the input, the output and the SLA before writing code (about the first 10% of the clock)
  - Decide what to delegate and what to own, and say it aloud ('the assistant scaffolds the data loader while I design the retrieval loop')
  - Audit AI output line by line; catching a hallucination scores higher than writing clean code from scratch
  - Harden at the end: time and space complexity, and failure modes such as a downstream API timeout
- **Red flags:**
  - 'Vibe coding': pasting giant prompts and accepting unverified output
  - Silent AI interaction
  - Cannot explain AI-generated code
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md), [Research Engineer / Member of Technical Staff](../02-roles/hubs/research-engineer.md), [Forward Deployed Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/forward-deployed-engineer.md), [Applied Scientist](../02-roles/hubs/applied-scientist.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md), [Research Scientist (AI/ML)](../02-roles/hubs/research-scientist.md), [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md), [AI Evaluation Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-evaluation-engineer.md), [GPU Kernel / ML Compiler Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/gpu-kernel-engineer.md), [AI Security Engineer / AI Red Teamer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-security-engineer.md), [Physical AI / Robotics AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/physical-ai-engineer.md), [Frontier AI Safety / Alignment Researcher](../02-roles/hubs/ai-safety-researcher.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md), [Responsible AI / AI Governance Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/responsible-ai-engineer.md)

- **Source:** Anthropic [C · T0-14 L171]
- **A strong answer covers** (from T0-14 L227, L243, L643, L803, L814; T1-03 L232):
  - A traffic estimate first: average and peak requests per second at 100x
  - Downstream failure handling: timeouts, retries and idempotency
  - Backpressure: a bounded queue that sheds load or returns 429 with retry-after, rather than unbounded queueing
  - Time and space complexity of the core logic
- **Red flags:**
  - Drops classic engineering (queues, retries, idempotency)
  - Over-engineers beyond the stated scale
- **Roles:** [AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-engineer.md), [Applied AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/applied-ai-engineer.md), [Agentic AI Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/agentic-ai-engineer.md), [AI Enablement Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-enablement-engineer.md), [AI Product Engineer (AI Frontend)](../02-roles/hubs/ai-product-engineer.md), [Forward Deployed Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/forward-deployed-engineer.md), [Machine Learning Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-engineer.md), [Research Engineer / Member of Technical Staff](../02-roles/hubs/research-engineer.md), [Inference / LLM Serving Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/inference-engineer.md), [ML Platform / MLOps Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ml-platform-engineer.md), [AI Infrastructure / GPU Platform Engineer](../02-roles/hubs/ai-infrastructure-engineer.md)
- **Skills probed:** APIs & integrations, System design, Python (production), Testing (pytest)

## System-design archetypes

The 15 recurring GenAI system-design archetypes ([T0-14](../../research/sessions/T0-14-ai-system-design-interview-patterns.md) §6.3). The [system-design guide](system-design-archetypes.md) has a case card for each.

| ID | Archetype | Family | Core tension | Staff-level tell | Most reported at | Prompts here |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Multi-tenant LLM inference API / serving platform | serving | Throughput versus latency; goodput under TTFT and TPOT SLOs | Defines the SLO as goodput (requests per second per GPU that meet both TTFT and TPOT) rather than raw throughput, ties capacity to KV-cache maths, and specifies tenant fairness and a canary rollout with an eval gate | Anthropic, OpenAI infrastructure, Google (C); B (41 Anthropic reports) | p023, p024 |
| A2 | GPU request-batching service | serving | Batch fill versus queue wait | Derives max wait from the latency budget, notes that continuous batching supersedes the timer design for generative workloads, and handles poison requests and cancellation | Anthropic (among the most reported prompts); B | p025 |
| A3 | Offline/async batch-inference API | serving | Using idle capacity versus protecting online SLOs | Treats price as a scheduling signal and batch work as the utilisation-smoothing layer for the fleet | Anthropic; B (12) | p026 |
| A4 | GPU fleet scheduling, placement, quotas/credits | serving | Bin-packing versus fairness versus cold-start cost | Derives placement constraints from weights plus KV memory, and notes that context length sets the concurrency ceiling | Anthropic, OpenAI; B (7 + 4) | p027, p028 |
| A5 | Model-weights distribution and safe rollout | serving | Source egress versus P2P complexity; rollback safety | Computes the distribution time before choosing a topology | Anthropic; B (16 + 2) | p029 |
| A6 | LLM gateway / internal AI platform | platform | Central control versus team autonomy; token-based limits | Uses organisation-level levers: a model-change policy with eval gates, cost attribution and exception handling | Listicles; Databricks-style platform teams; C | p030, p031 |
| A7 | Prompt playground / prompt registry and experimentation | platform | Versioning, streaming, multi-model fan-out cost | Closes the loop from playground to eval to CI gate to deployment ('prompts as code') | Anthropic, OpenAI; B (15) | p032 |
| A8 | Enterprise RAG / permission-aware search (including multimodal documents) | applications | Recall versus latency; ACL correctness; freshness | Treats ACL enforcement as a retrieval-time, fail-closed invariant, evaluates retrieval (recall@k) separately from generation (faithfulness), plans the embedding-model migration, and keeps untrusted content and sensitive data from meeting in one context without egress control (the EchoLeak lesson) | OpenAI, Databricks, Google, Anthropic (search over 1B documents); B/C | p001, p002, p003, p004, p017 |
| A9 | ChatGPT-style assistant with context assembly and memory | applications | Context budget versus quality; memory governance | Explains how prompt layout drives the prefix-cache hit rate and cost, and names memory governance (what is stored, who can delete it) | OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta ML; B/C | p005, p006 |
| A10 | Latency-critical code completion plus coding assistant | applications | Sub-second TTFT versus context quality | Pairs execution-based offline evals with online retention metrics and plans capacity for keystroke bursts | Meta ML pool, listicles; C | p007 |
| A11 | Long-running tool-using agent platform | applications | Autonomy versus blast radius; resumability | Designs the blast radius first (Rule of Two), makes tools idempotent and the loop resumable, and builds the eval harness before adding agent features | OpenAI (2026), Google agentic, Anthropic, scale-ups; C | p008, p009 |
| A12 | Real-time voice assistant | applications | End-to-end latency versus turn-taking correctness | States a per-stage p95 budget and overlaps stages (partial STT streamed into the LLM, sentences chunked into TTS) | PracHub ML-design pools, listicles; C | p010 |
| A13 | Document / multimodal ingestion and extraction at scale | applications | Cost versus accuracy; reprocessing on model change | Reasons in cost per correct document and versions outputs so a model or prompt change can be re-run safely | Databricks, listicles; C | p011 |
| A14 | LLM/agent evaluation platform and observability | cross-cutting | Grader trust versus cost; saturation | Sets an ownership model (the platform owns infrastructure, product teams contribute tasks) and links eval metrics to business outcomes | Anthropic (eval/monitoring and benchmark systems), Dataford GenAI-engineer aggregate, Staff+ listicles; B/C | p018, p035, p036, p037, p038 |
| A15 | Safety, abuse and prompt-injection defence architecture | cross-cutting | Containment versus usability; false positives | Designs for compromise: blast-radius analysis, kill switches, an audit trail and incident response | Anthropic (malware analysis, safety layer), OpenAI moderation, Databricks; B/C | p012, p013, p014 |

## Evidence and limits

- Prompts are quoted or closely paraphrased from what the research sessions report: T0-14 (firm table §6.2, archetypes §6.3, round formats §6.3b, the Dataford aggregate in K9), T1-03 (behavioural bank §6.2, coding formats §6.3) and T0-06 (applied-AI startup loops). The grade is that of the strongest report: B for aggregator tallies and coaching guides that T0-14 grades B (AceOffer's 112 Anthropic reports, Hello Interview); C for a single aggregator, review or listicle, and for the T1-03 synthesis; D where no prompt is reported, in which case reported_by says so and names the round description the prompt is built from. Variants named in reported_by may rest on weaker sources. Covers and red flags paraphrase the cited lines (T0-14 elicitation lists, trade-offs, Staff tells, formulas and rubrics; T1-03 STAR-AI and competencies C1–C4; T0-15 and T2-01 for the D-graded tracks), and answer_source lists those lines. They are coach-authored or synthesised criteria: no firm publishes an AI interview rubric (T0-14 K10; T1-03 §6.2). Role and skill keys are editorial (D): design prompts start from each role's interview track in data/role_scores.json and add roles whose reported loops include the prompt; behavioural prompts list every role whose skills-ontology links include each competency the question tests. Aggregator counts rank reported prompts; they do not measure prevalence or pass rates (T0-14 §7.1 O1, O12).
- No session measures pass rates by prompt, and no prep platform has independent outcome evidence [T1-03; T0-10]. Use the packs to practise the criteria, not to predict a loop.
- Data as of 2026-11-05. Loop formats and AI-tool policies change; re-check a company's current loop with its recruiter.
